title: Z2 direct-feed architecture, frozen before any new result

Z1.conversion: above the substrate, between substrate and die

Z2.crosses_substrate: 1 V supply and return only (after conversion)
Z2.conversion: below the substrate, inside the PCB cutout
power_path: HVR 48 V input terminals (VIN pad on the high-side RDL)
VR-to-substrate attach (Cu pillar + SnAg cap + underfill)

Z2BF.statement: This controlled experiment isolates the effect of BGA placement/cutout when both architectures are forced to use an identical package-level 48-V feed. It is not the primary Z2 construction.
Z2BF.geometry: identical to Z2 (attach + clearance); only the 48 V path differs
Z2BF.known_simplification: DEFECT #67: VIN modelled on the high-side RDL; the ~1.3 mm HV vertical traverse from the land-side RDL is not modelled (control only)

vr_attach.technology: Cu pillar + SnAg solder cap + underfill
vr_attach.pattern: VDD/GND checkerboard over each cell footprint
vr_attach.mechanical_convention: underfill-dominated card (as the interface microbump layer); column-stiffened Voigt card is a class-B bound
vr_attach.thermal_method: Voigt through thickness (Cu + solder columns in series), Maxwell-Garnett in plane (Phase 0M-R validated, <~0.6 % vs RVE)

sources.quote: 30μm pitch micro Cu pillar bump (15μm diameter) ... sufficient solder cap volume (16mm height)
bumps with a diameter of 30 µm, a height of 40 µm, and a space of 50 µm

direct_feed.definition: complete external 48 V supply + return loop between the board-level 48 V reference node common to both architectures (where Z1's PCB distribution meets its BGA pads) and the HVR input terminals, including the per-cell distribution to the 49 input terminals
direct_feed.heat_location_sensitivity: feed loss at the crossover R* deposited in the deepest converter tier
